post.caption: These gold bees may actually be wasps. It is a gold pendant of two insects that face each other. Their heads and tails are joined, and their wings spread back. Tiny gold balls and fine wire decorate it, and three small discs dangle from the wings and joined bodies. It is over 3,500 years old, from Minoan Crete, and it was found in 1930 at Chrysolakkos, near Malia on Crete. That place name means pit of gold. Researchers propose the insects are modeled on a large wasp, and the three discs may copy the fruits of a Cretan herb. It is in the Heraklion Archaeological Museum on Crete.
